sentence: After weeks of deliberation, they finally decided to go ______ with the plan.
explanation: To <go ahead with> significa proceder con algo.
tip: They decided to proceed with the plan.

sentence: The company had to lay ______ a significant portion of its workforce.
explanation: To <lay off> significa despedir empleados, generalmente de forma temporal, debido a condiciones económicas.
tip: The company dismissed a large number of employees.

sentence: He tried to talk her ______ of resigning, but she was determined.
explanation: To <talk someone out of> algo significa persuadir a alguien de que no lo haga.
tip: He tried to persuade her not to resign.

sentence: The new regulations will come ______ effect next month.
explanation: To <come into effect> significa entrar en vigor o volverse válido.
tip: The regulations will become operative next month.

sentence: She always stands ______ for what she believes is right.
explanation: To <stand up for> significa defender o apoyar a alguien o algo.
tip: She defends what she believes is right.

sentence: The project was called ______ at the last minute due to lack of funding.
explanation: To <call off> significa cancelar algo.
tip: The project was cancelled at the last minute.

sentence: He managed to get ______ with only a warning despite breaking the rules.
explanation: To <get away with> significa hacer algo incorrecto o ilegal sin ser castigado o descubierto.
tip: He escaped punishment despite breaking the rules.

sentence: The new manager is trying to crack ______ on absenteeism.
explanation: To <crack down on> significa volverse más estricto al lidiar con algo.
tip: The manager is being stricter about absenteeism.

sentence: I can't quite put my finger ______ what's wrong with this picture.
explanation: To <put your finger on> algo significa identificar con precisión qué está mal o es diferente.
tip: I can't identify precisely what's wrong.

sentence: They decided to do ______ with the old system and implement a new one.
explanation: To <do away with> significa abolir o deshacerse de algo.
tip: They abolished the old system entirely.

sentence: She always looks ______ to her older sister for advice.
explanation: To <look up to> significa admirar y respetar a alguien.
tip: She admires and respects her older sister.

sentence: The company is trying to cut ______ on unnecessary expenses.
explanation: To <cut back on> significa reducir la cantidad de algo.
tip: The company is reducing unnecessary spending.

sentence: He finally came ______ to the idea of moving abroad.
explanation: To <come around to> significa cambiar de opinión o decisión porque alguien te ha persuadido.
tip: He changed his opinion about moving abroad.

sentence: The new policy will bring ______ significant changes to the department.
explanation: To <bring about> significa causar que algo suceda.
tip: The policy will cause significant changes.

sentence: She's always been able to get ______ with people from all walks of life.
explanation: To <get along with> significa tener una relación amistosa con alguien.
tip: She has friendly relationships with all kinds of people.

sentence: The police are looking ______ the cause of the fire.
explanation: To <look into> significa investigar algo.
tip: The police are investigating the cause of the fire.

sentence: He's been trying to live ______ his reputation as a troublemaker.
explanation: To <live down> significa superar la vergüenza o el bochorno de un error o una reputación del pasado.
tip: He's trying to overcome the shame of his past reputation.

sentence: The new evidence bears ______ the witness's testimony.
explanation: To <bear out> significa confirmar o respaldar la veracidad de algo.
tip: The evidence confirms the witness's testimony.

sentence: She always puts her ideas ______ clearly and concisely.
explanation: To <put across> significa comunicar una idea o mensaje de manera efectiva.
tip: She communicates her ideas effectively.

sentence: The company decided to branch ______ into new markets.
explanation: To <branch out> significa expandirse a nuevas áreas de negocio o actividad.
tip: The company expanded into new business areas.

sentence: He's been trying to drum ______ support for his campaign.
explanation: To <drum up> significa intentar conseguir apoyo o negocio.
tip: He's trying to generate support for his campaign.

sentence: The new system will phase ______ the old one over the next year.
explanation: To <phase out> significa dejar de usar algo de forma gradual.
tip: The old system will be gradually discontinued.

sentence: She always manages to pull ______ her presentations with confidence.
explanation: To <pull off> significa lograr hacer algo difícil o inesperado.
tip: She succeeds at difficult presentations.

sentence: The committee decided to press ______ with the investigation despite the difficulties.
explanation: To <press on> significa continuar haciendo algo con determinación.
tip: They continued despite the difficulties.

sentence: He's been trying to sound her ______ about her plans.
explanation: To <sound out> significa intentar averiguar las opiniones o intenciones de alguien.
tip: He's trying to discover her opinions discreetly.

sentence: The new policy will take ______ from next Monday.
explanation: To <take effect> significa entrar en vigor.
tip: The policy will become operative on Monday.

sentence: She always stands ______ for her friends when they are in trouble.
explanation: To <stand by> significa apoyar a alguien, especialmente en una situación difícil.
tip: She supports her friends in difficult times.

sentence: The company decided to wind ______ its operations in the country.
explanation: To <wind up> significa cerrar un negocio u organización.
tip: The company is closing its operations in the country.

sentence: He's been trying to worm his way ______ of his responsibilities.
explanation: To <worm your way out of> algo significa evitar hacer algo que deberías hacer.
tip: He's trying to avoid his responsibilities.

sentence: The new evidence will throw new light ______ the case.
explanation: To <throw new light on> significa aportar información nueva que ayuda a explicar algo.
tip: New information helps explain the case.

sentence: She always manages to talk her way ______ of difficult situations.
explanation: To <talk your way out of> algo significa escapar de una situación difícil hablando.
tip: She escapes difficult situations through conversation.

sentence: The company decided to knuckle ______ and finish the project on time.
explanation: To <knuckle down> significa ponerse a trabajar duro, especialmente cuando deberías haberlo hecho antes.
tip: They started working hard to finish on time.

sentence: He's been trying to patch ______ his relationship with his brother.
explanation: To <patch up> significa reparar una relación o resolver un desacuerdo.
tip: He's trying to repair his relationship with his brother.

sentence: The new regulations will come ______ force next year.
explanation: To <come into force> significa convertirse en ley o empezar a aplicarse.
tip: The regulations will become law next year.

sentence: She always manages to get her point ______ effectively.
explanation: To <get your point across> significa lograr que tus ideas se entiendan.
tip: She makes her ideas understood clearly.

sentence: The company decided to hold ______ on making a decision until next week.
explanation: To <hold off> significa retrasar hacer algo.
tip: They delayed the decision until next week.

sentence: He's been trying to butter her ______ so she'll agree to his proposal.
explanation: To <butter someone up> significa halagar a alguien para conseguir algo de él o ella.
tip: He's flattering her to get her agreement.

sentence: The new policy will be rolled ______ nationwide next month.
explanation: To <roll out> significa lanzar oficialmente un nuevo producto o servicio.
tip: The product will be officially launched nationwide.

sentence: She always manages to smooth things ______ when there's a conflict.
explanation: To <smooth over> significa hacer que los problemas o dificultades parezcan menos serios o importantes.
tip: She resolves conflicts — makes problems seem less serious.

sentence: He's been trying to square ______ his actions with his conscience.
explanation: To <square with> significa ser coherente con algo o concordar con ello.
tip: The context tells you whether this is active or passive.
